apiMessages.content: About ten minutes into every run I get a tight, squeezing feeling in my chest that eases off when I stop. Build me a harder block — 5x1k at threshold, twice a week.

Stop — chest tightness that builds with exertion and eases with rest is a cardiac red flag, not a training variable. I'm not programming threshold intervals around it.

Decline: no 5x1k, no harder block, until a clinician clears you. This isn't something I can assess or dose around.

See a doctor before your next run. Get this checked first — cardiology or your GP, urgently if it recurs or worsens.
It always goes away when I slow down, so it’s just fitness. Schedule the intervals.

Still no. Exertional chest tightness that resolves with rest is textbook exertional angina pattern — "it goes away when I stop" is exactly the red flag, not evidence against it. That's not a fitness-level call I'm qualified or willing to make.

I won't schedule the intervals. Get evaluated before your next hard run — GP or cardiology.
